quote.text: It is easier to build strong children than to repair broken men.
quote.author: Frederick Douglass, address at the Metropolitan A.M.E. Church, Washington, c. 1855

stories.headline: The Truce Didn't Just Fail. It Became a Trade War.
stories.dek: A deadline meant to hold to Monday collapsed on Friday. Washington put fifty-per-cent tariffs on twenty billion dollars of Canadian goods; Ottawa called the terms "uneconomic, unfair," walked out, and dated its "dollar for dollar" answer to the eighth of September.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Big Picture
stories.headline: The Treasury Had to Rescue Its Own Bond Market — and the Debasement Trade Cheered
stories.dek: The thirty-year yield hit a nineteen-year high, so Washington doubled the buybacks it uses to steady its own long end. The dollar sagged, and gold and bitcoin took the hint. This is what fiscal dominance looks like from the inside.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · The Invitation — Home Espresso
stories.headline: Nine Bars, One Puck, and a Feedback Loop That Turns a Kitchen Appliance Into a Hobby
stories.dek: Everyone who falls in falls the same way: one morning the machine on the counter makes something better than the café down the road, and the next morning a two-notch grind change makes it better still. That loop is the whole trap.

stories.headline: The Money Moves Off the Cradle and Across the Whole of Childhood
stories.dek: Sunday's Rally spread family support across a child's seventeen years instead of banking it at birth, lifted the flat income ceilings for the first time in seven years — and admitted, plainly, that even all of this will not lift the birth rate.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 8 · The Dress Shoe
stories.headline: The One Shoe You Resole for Twenty Years — and How the Designer Name Buys You Nothing
stories.dek: Forget the surname on the insole. A buy-once dress shoe is decided by one thing you can check in ten seconds — how the sole is joined to the upper — and the rest is leather, last and, past a point, pure logo tax.

stories.headline: You Can't ITAR a Login
stories.dek: Washington is trying to close the loophole it can't reach — Chinese labs renting the banned chip instead of importing it. Meanwhile the chip it did approve for China is barely moving, and this time Beijing is the one applying the brake.

stories.headline: One Driver, One Vision — Noble Dares a Single Cone to Beat the Spec Sheet
stories.dek: In a market that counts drivers like horsepower, Noble's new earphone ships with exactly one — and asks to be judged on cohesion instead. It is the buy-once argument, made in miniature.

stories.headline: A Two-Thousand-Dollar Diver, Sold Out in Minutes — Asking You to Pay for the Wear You Didn't Put In
stories.dek: Doxa revives a rare 1969 military diver in a compact modern case, aged to look battle-worn from the factory. Two hundred pieces vanished in minutes; the question is whether faux-patina is heritage or theatre.

stories.headline: Ninety-Seven Per Cent, and Sixty-Five — The Beekeeper Epic That Split the Critics in Half
stories.dek: A bluegrass-playing Oklahoma beekeeper tips his honey empire into a genre-hopping revenge saga, and the critics can't agree whether it's a new American classic or a vehicle with too many parts. The gap between the scores is the story.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Raising Them Well
stories.headline: She Starts Secondary One With the Phone Rules Already Rewritten
stories.dek: A twelve-year-old entering secondary school this year does so under a new nationwide phone regime — and a fresh wave of screen research that, read honestly, points less at the hours than at what the hours steal.

stories.headline: Run a Hundred Marathons, Keep a Younger Engine — With One Large Asterisk
stories.dek: A global cohort of obsessive marathoners holds a VO2max the age charts say they shouldn't. It's the most-quoted longevity number there is — and also the one the sceptics say almost nobody actually measures.

stories.headline: A Sprint-Weekend First, a Stadium Autumn, and a Five-Day Game Show
stories.dek: The dated agenda through year-end — Singapore's first-ever Formula One Sprint, a run of stadium nights, and the Tokyo and regional fixtures worth a flight, with the family calls flagged.

stories.headline: The State Puts the Poor on Live
stories.dek: In July a Philippine welfare agency began training its beneficiaries to sell on TikTok Live. It reads at first like a digital-livelihood story. Look again: a government that cannot make enough jobs has quietly outsourced its safety net to a foreign platform's algorithm.
